analyst_view.overall: OFI Crete (16th, 6 pts) host Anderlecht (15th, 6 pts) in Heraklion, a straight fight for a play-off place between two sides on two wins from four. OFI arrive after a 0-2 home defeat to Panathinaikos and have a long injury list: striker Kenan Kodro, defender Kresimir Krizmanic, midfielders Fotis Koutsoupias and Konstantinos Lagoudakis, plus Chnaris and Marinakis; the numbers already count these. Anderlecht are unbeaten in four and won 1-0 at OH Leuven, where goalkeeper Colin Coosemans (foot) and striker Sikan played through knocks; they are without Lucas Hey and possibly Ilay Camara, both on the numbers' list, and travel on Wednesday despite a Greek general strike. Estonian referee Kristo Tohver, who has shown about 5.3 cards a game in his few matches on file, is in charge, which the numbers already count.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals and already take about 6% off OFI for Kodro and add about 6% to Anderlecht for Krizmanic missing at the back. Coosemans and Sikan playing through knocks is a small doubt for Anderlecht, but both played at the weekend, so I stay at 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, already up for OFI conceding many corners lately (35 in their last four). Nothing in the team news changes how either side attacks, so I stay at 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards and already add about 11% for referee Kristo Tohver's high card count (5.3 a game in six matches). A tight game for a play-off place could add a booking, but that is what the numbers already assume, so I stay at 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.4 shots, already lower for OFI's thin recent shooting (28 in four) and higher for Anderlecht's. That matches OFI's injury-hit midfield, so I stay at 26.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target, already raised for Anderlecht against an OFI side that has allowed 33 on target in six. Without new absences beyond what the numbers count, I stay at 9.7.
